title: Pass 1: Argument Flow, Section Headings & Transitions

content.quick: Structural editing ensures your thesis forms a continuous, unbroken chain of reasoning. Check heading hierarchy, cross-chapter narrative linkages, and ensure that every major claim is grounded in empirical or theoretical evidence.

sentences.text: Structural editing evaluates the overarching rhetorical architecture of an academic dissertation before granular phrasing is addressed.
sentences.simple: Structural editing means looking at the big picture of your thesis before worrying about spelling or small grammar mistakes.
sentences.plain: Structural editing evaluates the overarching rhetorical architecture of an academic dissertation before granular phrasing is addressed.
sentences.technical: Macro-structural manuscript appraisal prioritizes global argumentative coherence and teleological progression over localized micro-syntactic rectification.

visual.title: The Three-Tier Editing Hierarchy
visual.caption: Always edit from the top down. Fixing words in a chapter that needs deletion wastes hours.

sentences.text: Every section heading must accurately signal the analytical task performed in the text below it.
sentences.simple: Your subheadings must tell the reader exactly what is inside each section.
sentences.plain: Every section heading must accurately signal the analytical task performed in the text below it.
sentences.technical: Section taxonomic signifiers must exhibit rigorous functional mapping onto the empirical sub-routines executed within the corresponding textual unit.

visual.title: Pass 1 Structural Audit Checklist

items: Does Chapter 1 introduce every construct analyzed in Chapters 4 and 5?
Are all APA 7th heading levels strictly formatted (Level 1 Centered Bold, Level 2 Left Bold)?
Does the final paragraph of each chapter provide a bridge transition to the next?
Are chapter word counts balanced according to the university guidelines?

visual.caption: Verify all structural requirements before starting sentence-level editing.

questions.q: Why is it inefficient to correct punctuation and grammar before completing structural editing?
options: Because whole paragraphs or sections may be deleted or reorganized during structural revisions
Because grammar rules change between thesis chapters
Because punctuation does not matter in academic writing
questions.explanation: If a section is logically redundant and gets removed or rewritten during structural editing, any time spent polishing its commas is completely wasted.
